title: N4 sentence patterns with build and typing sentences

forms.name: May I …? / You may …
forms.note: The て-form plus もいいです gives or asks permission.
forms.trap: Do not use できます for permission: use てもいいです.
ex: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか。
May I take a photo here?
窓を開けてもいいです。
You may open the window.

forms.name: You must not …
forms.note: The て-form plus はいけません forbids something.
forms.trap: Do not use ないでください for a rule; it is a request.
ex: ここで食べてはいけません。
You must not eat here.
廊下を走ってはいけません。
You must not run in the corridor.

forms.name: Please do not …
forms.note: The ない-form plus で and ください asks someone not to do something.
forms.trap: Do not use ませんでください.
ex: ここで写真を撮らないでください。
Please do not take photos here.
心配しないでください。
Please do not worry.

forms.name: After doing …
forms.note: てから means after doing the first thing. The second action comes next.
forms.trap: Do not use から alone for “after”: the verb must be in て-form.
ex: 手を洗ってから食べます。
I wash my hands and then eat.
宿題をしてから寝ます。
I go to bed after doing my homework.

forms.name: Before doing …
forms.note: 前に follows the dictionary form: 寝る前に歯を磨きます. The tense of the sentence is given by the last verb.
forms.trap: Do not use the past form before 前に.
ex: 寝る前に歯を磨きます。
I brush my teeth before going to bed.
食べる前に手を洗います。
I wash my hands before eating.

forms.name: After doing … (た後で)
forms.note: た後で means after doing: ご飯を食べた後で歯を磨きます.
forms.trap: Do not use the dictionary form before 後で.
ex: ご飯を食べた後で歯を磨きます。
I brush my teeth after eating.
授業が終わった後で、友達に会います。
I will meet a friend after class.

forms.name: Have done … before
forms.note: The past form plus ことがあります means you have the experience of doing it.
forms.trap: Do not use the dictionary form: 行ったことがあります, not 行くことがあります.
ex: 日本へ行ったことがあります。
I have been to Japan.
寿司を食べたことがありますか。
Have you ever eaten sushi?

forms.name: Can do …
forms.note: The dictionary form plus ことができます means can do. It is more formal than the potential form.
forms.trap: Do not use the て-form: 泳ぐことができます.
ex: 私は泳ぐことができます。
I can swim.
ここで写真を撮ることができます。
You can take photos here.

forms.name: Intend to …
forms.note: The dictionary form plus つもりです says what you intend to do. The negative is ないつもりです.
forms.trap: Do not use つもり for something you have already done.
ex: 来年、日本へ行くつもりです。
I intend to go to Japan next year.
明日は早く寝るつもりです。
I intend to go to bed early tomorrow.

forms.name: Might …
forms.note: かもしれません means maybe or might. Use the plain form before it.
forms.trap: Do not add だ before かもしれません after a noun or a な-adjective.
ex: 明日は雨が降るかもしれません。
It might rain tomorrow.
この問題は難しいかもしれません。
This question might be difficult.

forms.name: Looks … (そう)
forms.note: Verb stem or adjective stem plus そうです means it looks like. おいしそう looks delicious.
forms.trap: Do not use the dictionary form before そう for appearance. For いい use よさそう.
ex: このケーキはおいしそうです。
This cake looks delicious.
雨が降りそうです。
It looks like it will rain.

forms.name: I heard that … (そうだ)
forms.note: The plain form plus そうです passes on what you heard.
forms.trap: Do not confuse it with the appearance そう, which follows the stem.
ex: 明日は雨が降るそうです。
I heard that it will rain tomorrow.
田中さんは先生だそうです。
I heard that Mr. Tanaka is a teacher.

forms.name: Seems that … (ようだ・みたい)
forms.note: ようです and みたいです say it seems that something is so, based on what you see or hear.
forms.trap: Do not use ようです for a plain wish or order.
ex: 田中さんは疲れているようです。
Mr. Tanaka seems to be tired.
外は寒いみたいです。
It seems cold outside.

forms.name: I think that …
forms.note: と思います gives your opinion. Use the plain form before と.
forms.trap: Do not use polite forms before と in the middle of a sentence.
ex: 明日は雨が降ると思います。
I think it will rain tomorrow.
この本は面白いと思います。
I think this book is interesting.

forms.name: Do things such as … and …
forms.note: たり … たりします lists examples of actions. The last verb carries the tense.
forms.trap: Do not use たり only once or with a different form.
ex: 休みの日は本を読んだり、映画を見たりします。
On days off I read books and watch movies.
週末は掃除をしたり洗濯をしたりします。
On weekends I clean and do the laundry.

forms.name: Too much
forms.note: Verb stem or adjective stem plus すぎます means too much: 食べすぎます.
forms.trap: Do not add すぎる to the dictionary form directly.
ex: 昨日は食べすぎました。
I ate too much yesterday.
この部屋は暑すぎます。
This room is too hot.

forms.name: Easy to … / hard to …
forms.note: Verb stem plus やすい means easy to do and にくい means hard to do.
forms.trap: Do not use the dictionary form before やすい.
ex: この辞書は使いやすいです。
This dictionary is easy to use.
この漢字は書きにくいです。
This kanji is hard to write.

forms.name: Must …
forms.note: なければなりません means must. Drop the い of ない and add ければ.
forms.trap: Do not use ません with ない: なければなりません.
ex: 毎日、薬を飲まなければなりません。
I must take medicine every day.
明日は早く起きなければなりません。
I must get up early tomorrow.

forms.name: Had better …
forms.note: た-form plus ほうがいいです gives advice. Use the ない-form for advice not to do.
forms.trap: Do not use the dictionary form before ほうがいい for positive advice.
ex: 早く寝たほうがいいです。
You had better go to bed early.
薬を飲んだほうがいいです。
You had better take medicine.

forms.name: If / when … (たら)
forms.note: たら means if or when something has happened. The result is not about a fixed rule.
forms.trap: Do not use たら for general truths; ば or と fit better.
ex: 雨が降ったら、家にいます。
If it rains, I will stay home.
駅に着いたら、電話してください。
When you arrive at the station, please call.

forms.name: If … (ば)
forms.note: The ば-form says that if one thing happens the result follows: 急げば間に合います.
forms.trap: Do not use ば for something that already happened.
ex: 急げば、電車に間に合います。
If you hurry, you will make the train.
安ければ、買います。
If it is cheap, I will buy it.

forms.name: Because … (ので)
forms.note: ので gives a reason in a soft, polite way. After a noun or a な-adjective it becomes なので.
forms.trap: Do not use ので for orders or requests in the main clause.
ex: 雨なので、家にいます。
Because it is raining, I will stay home.
忙しいので、行けません。
I am busy, so I cannot go.

forms.name: Although … (のに)
forms.note: のに means although and shows surprise or complaint.
forms.trap: Do not use のに when the result is expected.
ex: 勉強したのに、試験に落ちました。
Although I studied, I failed the exam.
春なのに、寒いです。
Although it is spring, it is cold.

forms.name: Do in advance (ておく)
forms.note: ておきます means do something in advance or leave it done.
forms.trap: Do not use ておく for what is already happening.
ex: 旅行の前に、ホテルを予約しておきます。
I book the hotel before the trip.
窓を開けておきます。
I will leave the window open.

forms.name: End up doing (てしまう)
forms.note: てしまいます means finish completely or do something by mistake.
forms.trap: Do not use てしまう for a plain action without regret or completion.
ex: 宿題を忘れてしまいました。
I forgot my homework (to my regret).
本を全部読んでしまいました。
I finished reading the whole book.

forms.name: Do for someone (てあげる・てくれる)
forms.note: てあげます is doing something for another person. てくれます is someone doing it for me.
forms.trap: Do not use てあげる for a superior; it sounds like a favour.
ex: 友達に本を貸してあげました。
I lent a book to a friend.
友達が手伝ってくれました。
A friend helped me.

forms.name: Can (potential verbs)
forms.note: Potential verbs: 食べられる, 書ける. The thing you can do often takes が.
forms.trap: Do not keep を with potential verbs in careful speech.
ex: 私は漢字が書けます。
I can write kanji.
朝は早く起きられます。
I can get up early in the morning.

forms.name: Let's / I will (よう)
forms.note: The plain volitional よう means let's or I will: 食べよう. ましょう is the polite form.
forms.trap: Do not use よう with a superior; use ましょう.
ex: 一緒に行こう。
Let's go together.
明日から早く起きよう。
I will get up early from tomorrow.

forms.name: When … (とき)
forms.note: とき means when. Use the plain form before it. After a noun use のとき and after a な-adjective use なとき.
forms.trap: Do not use polite forms before とき.
ex: 暇なとき、本を読みます。
When I am free, I read books.
駅に着いたとき、雨が降っていました。
When I arrived at the station, it was raining.

forms.name: While … (間に)
forms.note: 間に means during a period: 寝ている間に is while sleeping.
forms.trap: Do not use 間 and 間に as the same: 間に is for a one-time action within the period.
ex: 私が寝ている間に雨が降りました。
It rained while I was sleeping.
夏休みの間に日本語を勉強します。
I will study Japanese during the summer vacation.

forms.name: Explaining (んです)
forms.note: んです explains or asks for a reason: どうして休んだんですか.
forms.trap: Do not use んです for a plain statement of fact.
ex: どうして休んだんですか。
Why were you absent?
頭が痛いんです。
I have a headache (that is why).

forms.name: Make or let someone do
forms.note: The causative form says someone makes or lets another person do something: 食べさせる.
forms.trap: Do not use the causative for doing something yourself.
ex: 先生は学生に本を読ませます。
The teacher makes the students read a book.
母は私に野菜を食べさせました。
My mother made me eat vegetables.

forms.name: Should be … (はず)
forms.note: はずです means it should be so, based on a reason.
forms.trap: Do not use はず for a wish or a plan; use つもり.
ex: 田中さんは今日、来るはずです。
Mr. Tanaka should come today.
この問題は簡単なはずです。
This question should be easy.
